newsitem.title: FINLAND: VAN MIERT - COMPETITION CONCERNS IF NESTE, IVO MERGE.
newsitem.headline: VAN MIERT - COMPETITION CONCERNS IF NESTE, IVO MERGE.

text.p: European Commissioner for competition Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday the Commission would be likely to vet a merger between Finnish energy groups Neste Oy and Imatran Voima (IVO), if one went ahead.

"If it goes ahead, it is very likely we will have to scrutinise the case," Van Miert told a news conference during a two-day visit. "It cannot be excluded that on some elements of (a possible) deal, competition concerns might occur," he said.
Van Miert said he was simply indicating the need to look into such a case and identify the possible competition conerns, but it was too early to say any more about it.

The government, which controls both the oil, petrochemicals and gas group Neste Oy and national power grid IVO, said last week it was investigating broadening their ownership base and joint development, but so far there has been no word on whether the two will merge.

"Given the considerable market share of the electricity producer and adding to that the considerable potential of the gas side (of the business)... certainly for the industrial producers this could lead to some concern," Van Miert said.

"There is certainly no objection in principle (to such mergers), given that a lot of things are happening in the energy field," Van Miert said. "It is rather natural that mergers and acquisitions take place."
Van Miert said the main aim of his visit was to discuss competition matters, especially those related to the planned eastward expansion of the European Union.
Any new eastern European members would have to cope with competition and establish independent competition authorities, he said.
